A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DCBM. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and equations, tables and figures can be matched despite additions and relocation.

before.justification: V2 reports original classification accuracies, distribution-shift evaluations, localization measurements, runtime measurements and ablation results.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds dataset evaluations, data-efficiency experiments and concept-intervention outcomes.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix G.2 add optional text-guided concept removal: exclude cluster concepts exceeding a cosine-similarity threshold to a textual prompt, then retrain the classifier. The original proposal generation, clustering, projection, linear classifier and training loss remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V3 adds actual evaluation on AwA2 animal classification and CelebA face-attribute-combination classification with 110 classes (Appendices B.3 and F.2). This extends the evaluated populations and task requirements. AwA-related attribute labels in v2 served as detection prompts, rather than an evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: V3 adds published CelebA comparisons against CBM, ProbCBM, PCBM, CEM and ECBM, plus a BotCL comparison on an ImageNet subset. Figures 12–13 introduce explanation comparisons with CDM, LF-CBM and DN-CBM. The standalone ResNet-50 baseline disappears from the OOD comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 adds alternative 50-image concept subsets, their 100-image union, and classifier training restricted to 50 images per class. New evaluations specify AwA2/CelebA splits and preprocessing and a first-200-class ImageNet subset. The main OOD comparison switches to ViT-L/14, although DCBM results for that backbone already appeared in v2.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1 newly tests sensitivity to concept-subset selection and limited classifier-training data. Appendix G.2 tests removal of stone- and gull-related concepts, while G.3 adds comparative success and failure cases across CBMs and backbones. The existing background, PCA, clustering and hyperparameter ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without explicit repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. V3's alternative-subset experiment adds sensitivity evidence but does not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: CUB zero-shot accuracies change from 0.8/0.9/0.7 to 46.1/55.0/62.2 for RN50/B16/L14 (v2 Table 17; v3 Table 21). V3 adds data-efficiency, intervention and new-dataset results, plus DN-CBM's ViT-L/14 OOD errors. DCBM's ViT-L/14 OOD values in v3 Table 2 already appeared in v2 Table 19; they are not performance gains. The RN50 OOD results are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix A newly formalizes an object as a nonnegative weighted combination of concepts and states spatial-localization assumptions using image regions. This is a limited addition to the mathematical framing; Equations 1–3 remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: data-efficient generation of dataset-specific visual concepts, multiple granularities, fine-grained and OOD applicability, and localized explanations. V3's additional evidence and wording support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly separates concept-generation efficiency from classifier-training efficiency and qualifies textual concept names, CelebA label suitability and BotCL's backbone comparability. The OOD interpretation now emphasizes lower absolute errors under ViT-L/14. The previous inspection-only limitation is revised to acknowledge targeted concept removal.

D1.justification: V3 adds an explicit DCBM code-repository link, storage estimates, and AwA2/CelebA splitting, sampling and label-construction details. It documents intervention prompts and retraining, though the numerical removal threshold remains unspecified. Existing implementation, hardware, proposal hyperparameters and runtime descriptions are largely retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds discussion and citations concerning BotCL, self-explaining networks, energy-based and decoupling CBMs, and RAM. It explicitly contrasts constructing visual concepts with learning them. The central research positioning remains intact; several other reference changes merely update existing works to published versions.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most appendix prose remain intact. V3 makes targeted paragraph revisions, subdivides related work, renames Appendix A from Algorithms to Framework, introduces new appendix subsections, removes camera-ready editing notes and updates affiliations.

P2.justification: V3 adds substantial intervention and comparative-explanation displays in Figures 11–13 and new data-efficiency and benchmark tables. Figure 2 is enlarged and relabeled, the extended benchmark and Figure 10 are relocated, and OOD displays are reorganized. The earlier clustering plots and most ablation-table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 clarifies what data efficiency means and supports it with subset-selection and reduced-training-data experiments in Appendix A.1. Intervention examples, broader comparisons and added reproducibility details provide further benefits. The net gain is limited: RN50 OOD evidence is dropped, intervention thresholds remain unspecified, and the numerical mismatch between Table 4 and its accompanying discussion persists.
